neighbours.label: A word just after a frame of expectation ('fully expecting to be', 'hoping it was a', 'thought it would be a couple of'); the same words after a frame of plain knowledge or fact stay low.
fire: She flinched, fully expecting to be slapped.
We assumed it would be a matter of days.
They kept hoping it was a false alarm.
He was sure he was going to fail.
The crowd was expecting him to quit.
I figured it would be a waste of time.
Everyone had expected her to win easily.
We all thought it was going to rain.
quiet: She flinched, then sat down to be examined.
We learned it had been a matter of days.
They kept saying it was a false alarm.
He knew he was going to fail.
The crowd was cheering him on the stage.
I noticed it was a waste of paper.
Everyone had seen her win easily.
We all saw it was going to rain.

short: word after a frame of expectation
notes: Probes: 0.38-0.58 on the frames; 'hoped that she would lead a domestic life' 0.16, 'Hoping for a quick' 0.14. Plain sentences 0.01-0.03, 'knew that she would lead' 0.01. Often these expectations turn out wrong, but this test does not separate that.
